--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

(None)

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Unbounded product listing / browse endpoints
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (entire file)
Evidence: Repository contains product listing endpoints (products, all-products, explore-more-products) that are high-traffic browse routes and likely return large result sets; no schema/pagination proof available in-tree view. 
Impact: Without limits/cursor pagination these endpoints will cause full table scans and memory/timeouts as product count grows (painful by ~100k rows).
Fix: Enforce cursor or limit/offset pagination and return compact projections (avoid SELECT * on product table).

[DB-2] Multi-step checkout/payment flow split across routes
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts + src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (entire files)
Evidence: Payment flow is implemented across separate routes (create-order, confirm-order, verify-payment, razorpay-order, plus Razorpay webhook) which suggests multi-step writes touching orders, inventory, and payment records.
Impact: If writes are not wrapped in a DB transaction, partial failures (payment success vs order creation or inventory decrement) will create financial inconsistencies and inventory drift under normal load.
Fix: Wrap order creation, inventory decrement, and payment record writes in a single DB transaction (or design compensating transaction with idempotency and strong reconciliation).

[DB-3] Admin export / aggregate endpoints run full scans
File: src/app/api/admin/orders/export/route.ts (entire file)
Evidence: Presence of an admin orders export endpoint indicates potentially unbounded exports/aggregates over orders table.
Impact: Running exports or COUNT/SUM across the full orders table can spike DB CPU/memory and time out under large datasets (noticeable by ~100k rows).
Fix: Implement streaming exports, background batch jobs, and restrict/admin-rate the export with date filters and indexed WHERE clauses.

[DB-4] Likely N+1 on cart -> product resolution
File: src/app/api/cart/items/route.ts (entire file)
Evidence: Cart items endpoint exists separately from products endpoint (common anti-pattern: fetch cart rows then fetch product per item).
Impact: If the implementation fetches product details inside a loop per cart item, concurrent users will multiply DB calls (N+1) causing large query fanout at modest concurrency (~hundreds of concurrent users).
Fix: Fetch cart items with a single JOIN/include (or batch by product IDs) to avoid per-item DB roundtrips.

--- INFO ---

[DB-5] Prisma + Next.js connection pooling risk (requires confirmation)
File: src/lib/prisma.ts and prisma/schema.prisma (files present)
Evidence: Project uses Prisma (@prisma/client) in a Next.js app and contains src/lib/prisma.ts; file content couldn't be read to confirm singleton or pool usage.
Use: Verify src/lib/prisma.ts uses a cached singleton PrismaClient (module-level) for serverless or adds a pooled DB proxy (pgbouncer / RDS proxy) in production; otherwise expect connection exhaustion under serverless cold-start churn.
